messages:
jessica: Hey team — ACME-PROD hitting a steady stream of 429s since ~12:33. Dedicated pool not scaling up fast enough. min_replicas=2, max_replicas=20, warm_pool=4 but attach requests are queuing. Need fast eyes :exclamation:

samir: On it. Any deploys or infra changes in last hour?

jessica: No deploys. We saw a bunch of imagePullBackOffs earlier in ded-cluster-us-west2, some nodes re-booted for firmware patch at ~12:05.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2345 (auto-tag: dedicated-scaling). Pager duty alerted.

emily: Can you paste the autoscaler/controller logs around the scale events? Quick grep helps.

jessica: Here's the controller snippet:```
[scale-controller] 12:33:11 probe_sent tenant=acme-prod pod=acme-gen-abc status=probe_timeout reason=rate_limit
[scale-controller] 12:33:12 attach_request tenant=acme-prod warm_pool_id=wp-42 state=queued
[scale-controller] 12:33:20 probe_sent tenant=acme-prod pod=acme-gen-def status=probe_timeout reason=image_pull_backoff
[scale-controller] 12:33:45 scale_decision tenant=acme-prod desired=12 current=2 reason=queue_growth
[scale-controller] 12:34:15 scale_action tenant=acme-prod started=0 reason=resource_quota_failed rpc=attach_rate_limited
```

samir: Two interesting things: (1) probe timeouts with "reason=rate_limit" and (2) image_pull_backoff on some pods. Could be registry throttling + serialized warmpool attach causing the attach handshake to block.

mike: Also saw node_init_time spike to ~180s during that window (metric node.init.duration). That lengthens the attach path and increases concurrency on attach API which is rate-limited.

raja: I checked kubelet logs on one node: `kubelet: failed to pull image: 429 Too Many Requests -> registry rate limit` and later `kubelet: token refresh failed: 429`. Looks like ephemeral token refresh to registry is being throttled by our container registry partner after the firmware reboots caused many simultaneous pulls.

jessica: Repro steps I used locally: run load-generator with concurrency 400 to /v1/generate against acme-prod (dedicated). Header: `X-Redwood-Tenant: acme-prod`. Observed request queueing in front-proxy then 429s for ~8 minutes. Curl snippet:```
ab -n 20000 -c 400 -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Redwood-Tenant: acme-prod" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

emily: Short-term mitigations: (A) Increase min_replicas for acme-prod to 8 to give headroom for warm capacity, (B) temporarily relax autoscaler probe_rate_limit for dedicated clusters to allow more parallel attaches, (C) fallback to smaller model variant for burst traffic. I can roll A & C now if we agree.

samir: +1 to A and C. I'll file a quick runbook change to bump probe jitter and lower serialization window so attach requests don't latch serially.

mike: Long-term: we need to (1) harden registry rate-limit handling (stagger pulls, local cache), (2) add exponential backoff with jitter to attach handshake, and (3) surface a warmpool attach queue length metric per-tenant so we can signal earlier. I'll take ownership of those items.

raja: Also recommend adding a preflight check during node reboot windows to pre-pull hot model images to a subset of nodes so warmpool attachments don't rely on the global registry under load.

jessica: I told the customer we're applying temporary min_replica bump and enabling smaller-model fallback. They're OK with that while you triage. Will update after we confirm 429s subside.

ops-bot: Runbook action applied: bumped min_replicas -> 8 for tenant=acme-prod (auth: emily). Noted for rollback after incident.

samir: Action items: emily -> apply fallback + min_replica (done), mike -> investigate attach serialization & warmpool queue metric, raja -> registry token/backoff follow-up. I'll keep paged watches for 60m.

jessica: Thanks all. Notifying customer that mitigation is live. :thumbsup:
